A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete main text and Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image, layout, molecule, and unconditional-image generation experiments in Section 6, Tables 2–5, and supplementary experiments in Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their numerical and qualitative results, including the supplementary evaluations and ablations.

M1.justification: GRAFT, P-GRAFT, and inverse noise correction retain the same sampling, training, and inference procedures in Algorithms 1–7. Replacing PPO terminology does not change their algorithms or objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same tasks and datasets: GenAI-Bench, T2ICompBench++, and GenEval for text-to-image generation; PubLayNet for layouts; QM9 for molecules; and CelebA-HQ and LSUN-Church for unconditional images.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains SDv2, SDXL-Base, and DDPO. Appendix E.3 retains the same DDPO variants and PRDP evaluation discussion. Comparator membership in the layout, molecule, and flow-model experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices E–G retain the same splits, metrics, sampling settings, model configurations, training budgets, and testing procedures, including the 50,000-sample FID evaluation.

E4.justification: The conditional-variance analyses, Top-K/M sweeps, LoRA-rank tests, reverse stitching, molecule de-duplication and ReDeNoise ablations, compute analyses, and qualitative examples retain the same evidence.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains 1,000 repetitions with 100 rollouts. The uncertainty-reporting practice in Tables 2, 4, and 20 and matched-seed disclosures in Figures 5–6 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Main-text and appendix scores, rankings, curves, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, GenAI-trained P-GRAFT(0.25N) retains 71.94 ± 0.14 on GenAI-Bench in Table 2, and P-GRAFT(0.25N) retains QM9 stability of 92.61 ± 0.13 in Table 4.

T1.justification: Equation (1), the acceptance-function lemmas, bias-variance theory, and Appendix D proofs retain their mathematical content. Renaming p^ppo to p^RL and relabeling the unchanged optimization problem do not revise assumptions, derivations, or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution (a), and conclusion qualify GRAFT's claimed equivalence: v1 says it performs PPO, while v2 says it performs KL-regularized reward maximization with reshaped rewards. The other methodological and empirical contribution claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2 now distinguishes the KL-regularized objective from algorithms such as PPO used to solve it, refining the interpretation of GRAFT's optimization connection. Existing bias-variance explanations, experimental interpretations, and practical limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information remain unchanged, including Appendix E's LoRA and scheduler settings, Appendix F's sampling and training details, and Appendix G's architectures, checkpoints, and LSUN-Church noise perturbation.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Appendix A are unchanged, but the relationship to PPO is qualified: PPO becomes an example optimizer for the general KL-regularized objective rather than the procedure GRAFT claims to perform. The extra attribution to reference [7] repeats an existing citation.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites and subheading changes replace PPO terminology in the abstract, Sections 1–4 and 7, and Appendix D. Notation is updated accordingly, while section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Edited passages produce limited paragraph and equation reflow, particularly on pages 2–4, 16, and 18. Figures, tables, captions, and algorithm displays retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 more clearly distinguishes the KL-regularized objective from PPO as an optimization algorithm, bringing the abstract and conclusion into better alignment with the unchanged mathematics. This improves claim precision without changing the evidence. The correction remains incomplete: Lemma 4.2 still calls its objective PPO, and Appendices D.1 and D.3 introduce the wording 'RL regularized.'
